ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Information for Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Act No. 18619, as amended, effective Nov 1, 2024), Enforcement Decree of the Act (Presidential Decree No. 28633), Commercial Act (Act No. 17905, as amended), and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) regulations on beneficial ownership registration. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean FSC/KoFIU domestic sanctions list (including the Korean Consolidated Sanctions List). PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons as defined by FATF Recommendation 12, including immediate family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP or sanctioned individual, with ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening at least quarterly. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years post-relationship termination, per Article 7 of the AML Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Information System (I-Sa-Ro) – Commercial Registry Name Clearance Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) script, with the mandatory suffix '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa) for stock corporations. A parallel English trade name may be registered but does not replace the Korean statutory name. The name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) business type suffix, (2) distinctive trade name in Hangul, (3) object clause description, and (4) optional English transliteration. Phonetic transliteration of foreign names is permitted but must be consistent with the Korean Romanization system (Revised Romanization). Names that are identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names are rejected.

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written objection with the Commercial Registry Court (Bupwon) within 14 days of the rejection notice. The objection must include the proposed name, the rejection reason, and a legal argument demonstrating non-conflict with existing registrations. The court will review the objection within 7 business days and issue a binding decision. If the objection is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the High Court within 30 days. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a revised name application with a new distinctive token, which resets the 30-day reservation window. All appeals must be filed in Korean, with a certified translation if the applicant is non-resident.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Office), operating under the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Registration (beop-in deung-gi sincheongseo) submitted with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and required attachments to the competent court registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the Commercial Act of Korea. However, each issued share must have a par value of at least KRW 100 (or such lower amount expressly permitted by the Act), and the full subscription price of all issued shares must be deposited in a commercial bank before incorporation registration. No government-held blocked escrow account is required; instead, the deposit must be evidenced by a Capital Deposit Certificate issued by the bank, which cannot be withdrawn until the Company is duly registered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA (STOCK CORPORATION) ADOPTED ON [DATE] BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE FOUNDING DIRECTORS AT SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA. WHEREAS, the Company was organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), its Articles of Incorporation have been duly notarized, and all subscription consideration has been fully paid into a designated commercial bank in accordance with applicable statutory requirements; and WHEREAS, the founding directors desire to set forth the initial corporate governance and banking mandates and to establish the registered office, to effectuate the lawful operation of the Company's commercial stock photography, stock media marketplace, generative visual asset business and related AI licensing activities. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. Confirmation of Share Capital Subscription. The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription of [number] ordinary shares of par value KRW [par] each, for a total issued and paid-up capital of KRW [amount], which amount has been fully deposited with [Bank Name, Branch] and evidenced by the bank's Capital Deposit Certificate. The Representative Director is directed to maintain such certificate in the corporate book. 2. Adoption of the Registered Office. The Board adopts as the Company's registered office the premises located at [full address], Seoul, Republic of Korea, within the registration jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court. The Representative Director is authorized to execute and deliver the lease agreement, deposit, any security documents, and related covenants or arrangements for such premises. 3. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appoints [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, with exclusive authority to represent the Company in all ordinary and extraordinary business matters, and appoints [Name] as Director of Finance and Compliance. The Board further appoints [Name] as Auditor of the Company for a term of three years, commencing on the date of incorporation and expiring immediately prior to the annual shareholders' meeting for the third fiscal year thereafter. 4. Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the establishment of corporate current, checking, and payment collection accounts at [Bank, Branch]. Such accounts shall be operated under the joint signature of any two officers among the Representative Director and the Director of Finance and Compliance. The bank signature card, online banking enrollment, account authority matrix, and standing payment instructions are hereby approved. 5. Execution and Filing. The Representative Director is directed to file for corporate registration with the competent District Court Registry, register the business with the National Tax Service for corporate income tax, value-added tax and wage tax withholding, obtain all required internet and commerce-related certificates, and take all further steps to comply with Korean corporate law and to procure the final certificate of incorporation. 6. Certification. This resolution shall be effective as of the date of adoption and is binding upon the Company, all directors and officers, and their successors. Certified this [day] day of [month], [year]. [Name of Corporate Secretary], Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation of the Corporate Entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Supreme Court's iROS portal and use the Corporation Name Search and Reservation function. Enter the desired Korean name of the Chusik Hoesa, ensuring that the name is not identical to a previously registered name and does not contain prohibited trademark or governmental terms. The system will display any conflicting registrations; if the name is available, submit the reservation application, which will protect the name for six months. The incorporators must verify that the reserved name includes the mandatory suffix Chusik Hoesa or its English equivalent, and that all subsequent documents, including the notarized Articles of Incorporation, use the name exactly as reserved. For a foreign incorporator acting through an agent, upload a notarized power of attorney before the reservation is finalized.
required_dossiers: Online name reservation form
Passport or alien registration card of the incorporator
Notarized power of attorney (if an agent applies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the search identifies a conflicting name, the applicant must file a new reservation with up to two alternative names in the same session. If the reservation is suspended due to incomplete agent authorization, re-upload the notarized power of attorney and resubmit online. If a name is rejected for containing prohibited terms, revise the corporate name and reserve it again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public commissioned under the Korean Notary Act, usually located in the jurisdiction of the Seoul District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language in compliance with Articles 289 to 292 of the Commercial Act. The articles must state the exact corporate name, the full business purpose covering digital stock photography, visual asset marketplace, generation and licensing of AI-based visual content, the total authorized shares and par value, the number of shares subscribed by each incorporator, the registered office address, and the initial director and auditor provisions. A founding assembly of incorporators must be held unless all incorporators provide written consent to the draft articles. Thereafter, all incorporators, or their authorized attorney-in-fact, appear before the notary public to attest their signatures and the lawful nature of the articles. The notarized articles serve as the foundational governance instrument and are later attached to the incorporation registration application with the court registry.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the founding general meeting (unless waived by unanimous written consent)
Notarized consent forms of all incorporators
Valid identification documents of each incorporator
Power of attorney for any signatory acting on behalf of an incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies any defect or inconsistency in the articles, the incorporators must amend the document, obtain a fresh unanimous written consent, and appear again for notarization. If the articles are delayed due to incomplete identification, provide certified passport copies or alien registration certificates. Any material amendment after notarization requires a new notarial act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Shares and Deposit of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank) designated by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital deposit account in the name of the company-under-incorporation at the designated bank branch. All shares must be fully subscribed by the incorporators, and each subscriber must execute a share subscription statement declaring the number of shares and the amount subscribed. The entire subscription price for all subscribed shares must be remitted or physically deposited into the provisional account. The bank will verify the receipt of funds and issue a Capital Deposit Certificate (yeji jeungmyeongseo) indicating the depositor name, the deposited amount, the account number, and the confirmation date. This certificate must be attached to the incorporation registration application submitted to the court. The deposited funds may not be withdrawn or returned until the corporation has been legally registered and the provisional account is converted into the company's operating account.
required_dossiers: Provisional capital deposit account application form
Share subscription statements executed by each incorporator
Valid identification documents of all subscribers
Articles of Incorporation (for bank reference)
Remittance record or deposit slip for the subscription amount
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the Capital Deposit Certificate due to a mismatch between the provisional company name and the notarized articles, correct the bank account name and re-deposit the funds. If the deposit is rejected, transfer to another designated bank branch within the competent court's jurisdiction and obtain a fresh certificate. If the funds are returned by the bank to the subscriber, re-perform the deposit process completely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office (online: www.iros.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Corporation Registration (beop-in deung-gi sincheongseo) with the competent Registration Office within two weeks after receipt of the Capital Deposit Certificate and notarized Articles of Incorporation. Attach the notarized articles, the Capital Deposit Certificate, the founding meeting minutes, the written acceptance of office signed by each director and auditor, and the identity certificates of the statutory officers. Pay the registration tax, education surtax, and court issuance fee using the prescribed revenue stamps or the approved electronic payment system. The registrar will examine the dossier for statutory compliance; upon approval, the Company is created as a juridical person and an official Certificate of Corporate Registration (hoesa deung-gi sahang jeungmyeongseo) is issued. No commercial operations, bank account finalization, or contract execution may lawfully occur before this certificate is obtained.
required_dossiers: Application for Corporation Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital Deposit Certificate issued by the bank
Minutes of the constituent general meeting
Appointment acceptance statements of directors and auditor
Identity certificates of all directors and auditor
Power of attorney (if a representative files on behalf of the company)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary instruction (bomanmyeongryeong) or temporarily suspends the application, furnish the requested documents within the statutory cure period, generally fourteen days. If the application is rejected, acquire the missing documents or amend the defective provisions, then file a new application. The incorporators may also contest the disposition by filing an immediate motion under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within the prescribed statutory window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Bank Account Activation and Post-Incorporation Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (Seoul Regional Tax Office) and the local municipal tax branch; commercial bank where the provisional capital account was opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days of receiving the court-issued incorporation certificate, the Representative Director or the designated agent must register the Company for tax purposes by submitting the Business Registration Application to the competent National Tax Service office. The NTS will issue a Business Registration Certificate, which is indispensable for issuing tax invoices, executing contracts, opening the final corporate bank account, and integrating payment service providers such as Stripe or PayPal. The provisional capital deposit account must be converted into the Company's regular operating account in the presence of the authorized joint signatories. The Board must then execute the final bank signature card, issue share certificates to each subscriber, and record the statutory beneficial ownership registers. If any shareholder is a non-resident, a Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and intervention notifications under Korean foreign exchange regulations must be filed with the designated authorities.
required_dossiers: Official corporate registration certificate from the court
Business Registration Application Form (NTS)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or ownership document for the registered office
Identification cards of the Representative Director and directors
Bank account conversion form and joint signature cards
Foreign investment report (if non-resident shareholders are present)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS demands supplemental materials, provide the requested documents through the HomeTax system (www.hometax.go.kr) within ten days and coordinate with the assigned case officer. If the bank refuses to convert the provisional account due to unclear beneficial ownership, submit a shareholder declaration, a court transcript, and the Business Registration Certificate to the bank's compliance desk. Any delay in foreign investment notification must be cured by filing an amended report promptly, along with payment of any applicable late-filing penalty.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) at www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa, the entity must first complete corporate registration at the competent local District Court, obtaining the Corporate Registration Number. Thereafter, the legal representative or designated local tax representative must apply for a Business Registration Number (BRN; TIN and VAT registration) with the competent district tax office or via the Home Tax Service portal within 20 days of business commencement. The required documents include the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, lease agreement for the local place of business, identification document of the representative, power of attorney and registration evidence for the tax representative (where applicable), and bank certificate evidencing the paid-in capital. The NTS issues the Business Registration Number in real time upon online submission through HTS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not permit check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; the Chusik Hoesa is automatically taxed as a resident corporation under the Corporate Tax Act, subject to worldwide income taxation with no transparent pass-through alternative.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) as enacted under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 0 KRW (no turnover exemption for corporations; every domestic supply of goods or services by a Chusik Hoesa mandates VAT registration effective from business inception)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered persons must issue a mandatory electronic tax invoice (Jeonja Sesyeo) through the NTS Home Tax Service within the day following the supply date. The electronic invoice must be transmitted to the NTS using the prescribed API/HTS interface and must contain the transaction certificate number, anti-fraud surrogate key, taxable amount, VAT amount, and the Business Registration Numbers of both parties. Paper tax invoices are permitted only with explicit NTS approval and are subject to strict issuance deadline rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Qualifying foreign exchange-earning services, including cross-border licensing of digital stock media and stock photography to foreign users, are zero-rated when the service is deemed supplied to a foreign country, payment is received in convertible and freely transferable foreign currency, and the foreign currency is repatriated into South Korea. The Chusik Hoesa must maintain evidence of foreign counterparty identity, supply and licensing contracts, proof of actual performance or digital delivery, and final receipt of foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration No. / Export Confirmation issued by the Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill/Electronic Transport Document for digital freight or accompanying physical media)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean bank, evidencing the receipt and repatriation of foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines that the zero-rated export was false, unverifiable, or failed to meet the foreign exchange repatriation deadline, it may reassess VAT at the standard 10% rate, impose additional tax penalties of up to 40% of the evaded tax for fraudulent or grossly negligent filing, and apply negligence surcharges under the National Tax Basic Act and the Value-Added Tax Act. The filing of false export documentation can trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine not exceeding 20 million KRW, and the clawback of any VAT input tax credits or refunds already claimed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) exercising supervisory authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized but declaration-heavy foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The Korean won is convertible for current account trade and service flows, which include stock-photo licensing and subscription fees; these settlements may be carried out freely through a designated foreign exchange bank, with reporting on a post-transaction basis. Capital account transactions, however, require express reporting or approval; the full subscription of shares by non-resident beneficial owners is classified as foreign direct investment and requires filing with the designated bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Export proceeds are subject to a settlement accounting deadline, but Korea does not require compulsory surrender to the central bank. A company may keep receipts in a foreign currency deposit account or convert them into Korean won at the market rate. Profit remittance is permitted once audited retained earnings exist, the dividend distribution is reported, bank-level verification is completed, and Korean withholding tax is paid. The won in practice is settled onshore only, with offshore non-deliverable forwards as the standard synthetic hedge for non-residents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act export settlement regulations, service and digital asset export proceeds must be received within the contractually agreed payment due date, or within 18 months from the export declaration/invoice date when no specific contract date exists; receipt must occur through a designated foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: the Chusik Hoesa may retain 100% of the foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account, or elect to convert to Korean won at the prevailing market rate. All export receipts must be filed against the company's trade settlement ledger, and any receipt routed through third-party wallets without an underlying service invoice will be reported as an FX procedural violation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Legally barred as the sole corporate treasury spine. Under the Banking Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, only licensed banks may receive deposits and provide foreign exchange settlement for Korean entities. Offshore fintech EMIs - including Wise Business, Revolut Business, and Stripe Treasury - can support settlement between the platform and overseas photographers, but they cannot act as the Korean Chusik Hoesa's designated foreign exchange bank for Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting, capital contribution verification, or KRW clearing. Using an unlicensed EMI as the operational treasury creates FATF compliance vacancies, unmapped transaction trails, and a likely rejection of the foreign-investment report. Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury rail, Medium as an ancillary receivables collection rail only if a full domestic bank account is maintained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks apply the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act strictly to corporate accounts. The statutory representative and, in the case of foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa, the non-resident ultimate beneficial owner, must generally appear in person at an in-branch financial transaction interview. Remote consular proxy opening is technically possible only with a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney, under which an appointed proxy appears physically at the Korean branch with the director's passport, confirms the beneficial-ownership chain, and answers compliance officer questions by video link. In practice, tier-1 banks require at least one in-person interview before activating FX clearing and overseas remittance services; fully digital onboarding without any physical footprint is not acceptable for a foreign-invested stock photo company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend/profit remittance directed to a non-tax-resident shareholder in a jurisdiction with incomplete tax transparency, raising tax evasion and proceeds-of-crime concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder minutes approving the dividend; audited financial statements with retained earnings calculation; Korean withholding tax payment receipts; certified tax-residence certificate of the recipient; annual corporate tax returns; banking history proving a prior established relationship with the beneficiary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the non-resident investor's transfer via SWIFT MT103 into the Chusik Hoesa's foreign currency deposit account at the designated tier-1 bank. Before funds arrival, the investor must file a Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through the designated bank, and on receipt the bank issues a Foreign Exchange Purchase/Sale Certificate and the company registers as a foreign-invested entity. The remitter must be the legal shareholder, no third-party payments are acceptable, and the transfer currency must be freely convertible (USD, EUR, JPY, GBP). A certified public accountant performs the capital verification before the capital escrow balance is released for stock photo platform operating costs. The remittance should state the exact purpose code for ordinary acquisition of shares under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for high-value royalty, licensing, and distribution payments to overseas photographers and AI artists; MT202 is used only for interbank USD settlement when instructed by a correspondent. A Commercial Letter of Credit is structurally inappropriate for digital stock-photo template sales and should be reserved for physical production, hardware, or tangible media deliverables. Documentary collections are acceptable only when the counterparty requires proof of delivery; for AI digital assets, append the license invoice, download-settlement log, and customer acceptance record to the payment instruction. Korean Won clearing is executed by the Bank of Korea real-time settlement system at the designated bank, with all outbound remittances subject to bank FX declaration reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KFTC (Korean Foreign Exchange Forward) contracts on USD/KRW up to 12 months with real and documented service-export forecasts
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW permitted for non-resident shareholders hedging Korean won economic exposure, settled in USD without onshore KRW delivery
Cross-currency swaps between the Chusik Hoesa and a licensed Korean bank for long-term foreign-investment funding, allowed only with underlying FDI or debt documentation
Plain-vanilla FX options and request-for-quote forwards linked to specific stock-photo licensing invoices, strictly excluding speculative naked positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general shareholders' meeting and approval of the statutory financial statements, including the balance sheet, income statement, statement of appropriation of retained earnings and notes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ of the Chusik Hoesa; minutes entered in the corporate minute book and made available to shareholders and the court registry on demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31 of the following year. A court extension is available only in extraordinary circumstances.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare or present statutory financial statements or who fail to convene the ordinary general meeting within the statutory window are exposed to administrative fines under the Commercial Act of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700); the court may compel convening of the meeting, and the absence of approved financial statements invalidates the annual registry report.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate report (annual return) filed in the commercial register, containing registered share capital, directors, auditors, and the accounting and audit summary documents required by the Commercial Registration Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Court Registry Office (Commercial Registration Section) for the jurisdiction of the company's principal registered office in South Korea.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, by April 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a court order to comply and administrative fines; if a corporation remains in default for five consecutive annual report cycles, the Commercial Act permits the court to dissolve it after public notice as a dormant corporation, leading to administrative strike-off and forfeiture of registered corporate capacity unless a creditor or shareholder timely petitions for revival.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax final return and self-assessment for the fiscal year, including tax base calculation, earnings and profits adjustments, tax credits, foreign tax credit items, and payment of any balance corporate tax due.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS); filed through the HomeTax electronic portal with the competent regional tax office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year company, generally by March 31. If the return is prepared and signed by a certified tax accountant or the corporation is subject to external audit, the filing due date is extended to April 30 under the Corporate Tax Act, with a corresponding extension of the tax settlement date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of the unfiled corporate tax; under-reported tax triggers 10% additional tax, increasing to 20% for intentional underreporting or aggravated omission; overdue corporate tax accrues statutory daily interest of approximately 0.022% per day, adjusted quarterly by NTS. Persistent non-payment allows NTS to impose tax liens, seize bank accounts and receivables, and auction assets; prolonged failure also supports the dormant-company removal process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment equal to 10% of the national corporate tax for the same fiscal year, filed with the provincial or municipal tax administration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government with jurisdiction over the registered business place (special self-governing province, metropolitan city, si, gun, or gu), using Wetax or the local tax e-filing system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax window, within three months after the fiscal year end; March 31 for calendar-year companies unless the national return extension adjusts the local due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Local Tax Act imposes a non-filing penalty of 20% of assessed local tax, an understatement penalty of 10%, and statutory overdue interest; the local government may attach real property and bank accounts and conduct a public auction to collect unpaid local corporate income tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external auditor's report and audited financial statements prepared by a certified public accountant registered with the Financial Supervisory Service; the audit report is presented to shareholders and annexed to the commercial registry annual report where required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART for external-audited companies; the court registry also receives the approved audited financial statements through the annual corporate report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit must be completed before the ordinary general meeting, which for a calendar-year company is normally by late March; audited financial statements must be filed with FSS within two weeks after the shareholders' approval, and by the April 30 annual registry report deadline in practice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Act on External Audit of Stock Companies imposes administrative measures against the external auditor, suspension of the audit deficiency designation, and criminal fines or imprisonment for false audit opinions; a mandatory-audit company's registry annual report may be rejected if the audit opinion is missing, and sustained default can lead to commercial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Overseas financial account report covering the corporation's Stripe and PayPal settlement accounts, merchant accounts, virtual accounts, foreign bank deposits, and other foreign financial assets held outside Korea.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (the taxpayer's competent regional tax office) as the central competent authority for offshore financial account reporting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By June 30 of the year following any calendar year or month in which the aggregate balance of the corporation's foreign financial accounts exceeds KRW 500 million.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or underreporting foreign financial account balances is subject to penalties under the tax and financial-transaction regulatory framework: up to 20% of the undisclosed balance for negligent failure and up to 30% or KRW 200 million for intentional failure; aggravated intentional concealment of balances above KRW 5 billion may carry criminal imprisonment of up to two years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual register audit and refresh of the shareholders' register, director register, auditor register, charge register and minute book; updating share transfers and changes in beneficial or shareholder information in the corporate books.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company head office, board and legal representative; no external filing in a no-change year, but foreign-investment changes are reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through a designated foreign-exchange bank.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous upon occurrence; the corporate secretarial register audit is completed annually at or before the AGM; share transfers must be registered in the shareholders' register to be valid against the company; foreign-investment changes are reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unregistered transferee cannot exercise shareholder rights; false register entries expose the responsible director and officer to fines up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act; violations of foreign-investment reporting can trigger penalties under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; and false corporate records may invalidate the annual registry report.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered by the balance-sheet total asset test of KRW 12 billion or more at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, approximately USD 9.2 million at KRW 1,300/USD; no separate revenue or headcount threshold exists under Korean general corporate law. In addition, listed companies and companies whose securities are traded on a Korean exchange, financial companies and investment institutions, and companies designated by FSS for public-interest reasons are subject to mandatory external audit irrespective of total assets. A newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa applies the total-asset test based on its first fiscal-year balance sheet.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements for mandatory-audit public-interest entities must use K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards); non-public corporations subject to external audit may prepare their financial statements under K-GAAP (General Enterprise Accounting Standards) unless they voluntarily apply K-IFRS; corporations below the external-audit threshold may use SME or simplified accounting standards for bookkeeping and must maintain tax-basis accounting records under the Corporate Tax Act. Statutory audit opinions are issued by Korean CPAs under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean private law does not impose a separate annual UBO declaration on a non-listed Chusik Hoesa; the entity confirms and records beneficial ownership through the registered shareholder ledger and statutory registers. Any share transfer must be entered in the Register of Members before the transferee can exercise shareholder rights. If a transaction triggers foreign investment or a foreign investor changes equity, a report or change notification must be given to MOTIE through a designated foreign-exchange bank within 30 days. For banking and payment-rail onboarding, including Stripe and PayPal settlement accounts, the financial institution must verify beneficial owners and may require annual reconfirmation under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and the AML framework.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Statutory Auditors / Audit Committee Members
Commercial books and material records (journal, ledger, receipts, contracts)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year; typical Korean registered-office, legal agent and corporate secretarial service provider range.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a statutory audit of a medium non-public corporation; voluntary review or attestation below the statutory threshold generally ranges from USD 3,000 to USD 8,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: South Korean corporate income tax is progressive: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on the excess up to KRW 20 billion; 21% on the excess up to KRW 300 billion; and 24% on the excess over KRW 300 billion; plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax liability.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general patent box applies to stock photography licensing; however, qualifying AI R&D expenses entitle the entity to tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act (25%-50% for National Strategic Technologies and up to 40%-50% of qualifying R&D for SMEs); a foreign-invested high-tech stock-photo/AI enterprise may obtain a 100%/50% corporate income tax holiday for 3-5 years plus a 50% reduction for two additional years in a Free Economic Zone under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; job-creation and facility-investment tax credits are also available to lower the effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporation Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Schedule) and attachment schedules, filed electronically through the National Tax Service Home Tax System (Hometax) at www.hometax.go.kr; non-resident payees are reported through the withholding tax reports on the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations that paid corporate tax of more than KRW 5 million in the immediately preceding year must also file an interim provisional tax return within two months after the expiry of the first six months of the current fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the closing date of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is March 31 of the next taxable year, extended to the next business day if the date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification, registration number, close of books, head office location, place of effective management, shareholder identity, and foreign investment status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the company is a Korean tax resident because its place of effective management is in Korea even if 100% owned by non-residents; every non-resident director and shareholder must have a foreign tax identification number and resident address stated; compensation for a non-resident director's Korean services must be withheld at the statutory non-resident WHT rate unless a DTA claim is properly documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening balance sheet assets and capital, paid-in capital, statutory appropriation, and issuance of shares; for an online stock-photo company, intangible assets and AI model capitalization are separately disclosed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Equity contributed by a foreign parent must be evidenced by currency payment records through foreign exchange; a shareholder loan from a non-resident parent is subject to Korean thin capitalization limitation of 3:1 debt-to-equity for controlling foreign shareholders, and excess interest may be recharacterized as dividend subject to 22% WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, subscription revenue, licensing revenue, AI-generated visual asset sales, commission revenue, and operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all global revenue derived by this Korean stock corporation, including revenue in JPY, USD, and EUR converted into KRW at the official exchange rate on the date of receipt or at the fiscal-year-end book rate; revenue sourced through foreign platforms remains taxable to the Korean resident company as worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, nondeductible expenses, tax-base adjustments, reserves, depreciation on servers and equipment, and research-development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reject deductions for fines, corporate income taxes, excessive entertainment costs, and unjustified management fees paid to the foreign parent; expenses supported only by invoices from a non-resident related party require proof of actual services and an arm's-length benefit to the Korean business; intercompany payments must be supported by service agreements, workpapers, and evidence of active AI development in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward, loss contingency reserves, and tax-exempt income or statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A carryforward loss can be deducted only if the ownership and business identity remain substantially unchanged and proper evidence of the loss year is filed; a change of non-resident shareholders above 50% may extinguish loss carryforwards unless the same business continues in a manner satisfying Korean tax law; the deducted amount is capped by statutory limitations for large companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: foreign tax credit, R&D tax credit, job creation tax credit, investment tax credit, and dividend-received deduction for inbound dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If royalties for stock-photo sales are subjected to foreign withholding taxes, claim a foreign tax credit under the Corporate Tax Act in the Korean return; R&D credits for AI photo-indexing, computer-vision, and image-processing algorithms must be supported by payroll records, technical records, and dedicated time reports; do not claim treaty benefits directly against Korean corporate tax unless lawfully available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of national corporate tax at progressive rates and local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%/19%/21%/24% brackets to taxable income and add local income tax equal to 10% of national corporate tax; non-resident corporate shareholders are not taxed at this box, but retained earnings will be subject to Korean withholding tax upon actual distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional taxes, penalties, prepaid taxes, withholding reconciliation, and non-resident payments schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents on the withholding reconciliation schedule; compute statutory WHT at 22% combined, then apply treaty-reduced rates only upon valid Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial-ownership forms; unpaid WHT and unsubmitted withholding forms trigger additional taxes and may void deduction of the related payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of the annual return triggers a 20% additional tax on the unpaid national corporate income tax, rising to 40% for fraudulent or dishonest omission, plus a daily overdue surcharge of approximately 0.022% per day on the delinquent amount; local income tax surcharges are additionally imposed; failure to file or remit withholding taxes triggers 10%-20% additional tax; deliberate concealment may be prosecuted under the Punishment for Tax Offenses Act with imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% combined on dividends distributed to a non-resident shareholder: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, unless reduced under a DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident company seeking treaty relief must, before or no later than the date of each dividend, royalty, or interest payment, submit to the Korean withholding agent: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence state issued for the calendar year in which the payment is made; (2) a signed application for tax exemption or reduction under the applicable bilateral tax treaty, submitted through Hometax; (3) a beneficial ownership statement confirming that the recipient is not a conduit and has the right to use and enjoy the payment; and (4) confirmation that the recipient has no permanent establishment in Korea. If the documents are not completed by the payment date, the payor must withhold at 22% and the recipient may later claim a refund through a corrective assessment; the payor must retain the TRC and treaty claim in the withholding records for at least five years, and DTA eligibility is tested under the Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is also 22% combined (20% national plus 2% local). Treaty-reduced rates in Korea's DTAs commonly provide 5%-15% for dividends, 10%-15% for interest, and 10%-15% for royalties; for example, under the Korea-US DTA, portfolio dividends are generally 15%, direct dividends to a 10% corporate shareholder are 10%, interest is generally 10%, and royalties are 15%, depending on the applicable treaty version. Non-arm's-length royalty paid to a low-tax jurisdiction may be disallowed and recharacterized as a constructive dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border related-party transactions with a total annual value of KRW 10 billion or more require comprehensive transfer pricing documentation, including Local File and Master File, in Korea; simplified documentation may be required where transactions exceed KRW 5
